We compare free-form vs.

items.title: Spatial DJ: Spatial Audio Control for Arbitrary Loudspeaker Layouts
items.summary: We present Spatial DJ, a system for on-site loudspeaker layout acquisition and real-time spatial audio rendering and control, using head-worn AR in a coordinate frame aligned to the physical loudspeakers.

items.title: SPHERE: A Multi-Attribute No-Reference metric for Binaural Speech Quality And Spatial Fidelity
items.summary: In this paper, we introduce SPHERE (Spatial and Perceptual Human Evaluation and Rating Estimator), a multidimensional no-reference perceptual evaluation framework for binaural speech. SPHERE defines nine distinct perceptual and spatial attributes that characterize the immersive listening experience.

items.title: One Waveform, Two Stories: Benchmarking Speech-Acoustic Conflict in Audio-Language Models
items.summary: Audio-language models (ALMs) are evaluated on their understanding of both speech and environmental sounds. We introduce SAC-Bench, a benchmark of intra-audio speech--acoustic conflict comprising 616,031 unique clips from 188 sound-event classes across seven semantic, temporal, and spatial tasks.

items.title: SPATEX: Array-Flexible Multichannel-to-Multichannel Target Speech Extraction using Direction Clue
items.summary: Multichannel-to-multichannel target speech extraction (MIMO TSE) aims to recover the target speech signal at each microphone while preserving interchannel spatial information. In this work, we propose SPATEX, the first array-flexible MIMO TSE framework that reconstructs microphone-wise target speech signals across microphone counts and array geometries.

items.title: Zero-Shot Voice Cloning for Synthetic Data Augmentation in Children's ASR
items.summary: Children's automatic speech recognition (ASR) lags behind adult ASR due to theacoustic mismatch between adult-trained acoustic models and children's speech, as well as the scarcity of labelled children's speech corpora.

items.title: A Compact Statistical View of Musical-Instrument Directivity
items.summary: Directivity is a defining feature of musical-instrument radiation and is known to vary strongly with frequency. With the growing availability of measured directivity datasets and their use in sound-field simulation and spatial audio, there is a practical need for representations that are both compact and comparable across sources.

items.title: Sequence-to-Sequence Refinement for EEND-VC Diarization with a Shared Encoder
items.summary: End-to-end neural diarization with vector clustering (EEND-VC) separates local segmentation from global speaker assignment, leaving speaker confusion (SC) despite strong segmentation. We study frozen-feature refinement with WavLM and structurally pruned w2v-BERT 2.0, and extend the latter to joint training of local segmentation and refinement heads.

items.title: How Much Prosody Does Your ASR Encoder Already Know
items.summary: Traditional detectors rely on hand-built prosodic features (pitch, speaking rate, pauses), while modern detectors run on a neural ASR encoder that has processed the same audio. Second, we test whether prosody can be recovered from the encoder. The three tests agree; prosody adds a large gain on raw audio, but that gain collapses once the signal passes through even the first encoder layer.

items.title: Count-Density Networks for Modal Plate Parameter Estimation
items.summary: We describe two submissions to Task B of the 1st DAFx Parameter Estimation Challenge, which estimates an unknown number of modal frequency, decay, and gain triples from a synthetic plate-reverb impulse response.

items.title: Understanding the relationship between retrospective soundscape attributes and continuous pleasantness and eventfulness ratings
items.summary: Soundscape studies ask listeners to rate perceived affective quality (PAQ) attributes, such as pleasant and vibrant, after listening to recordings or experiencing acoustic environments. International Organization for Standardization (ISO) procedures convert these PAQ ratings into Pleasantness and Eventfulness scores.

items.title: Continual Residual Memory for Gradient-Free Test-Time Adaptation in Speech Enhancement
items.summary: Test-time adaptation (TTA) addresses this problem using unlabeled test observations, but existing approaches mainly rely on online parameter optimization and do not explicitly exploit the residual discarded by the enhancement backbone. We propose Continual Residual Memory (CRM), a gradient-free continual TTA framework for selective residual recovery.

items.title: Multilingual TASU: Extending Text-Only Alignment to Multilingual Speech Recognition via Simulated CTC Posteriors
items.summary: Speech Large Language Models (Speech LLMs) achieve strong multilingual ASR when large-scale paired speech-text data is available, yet such resources remain scarce and highly imbalanced across languages. In this work, we investigate TASU-style posterior alignment as a means of mitigating paired-data scarcity in multilingual ASR.

items.title: Learning Timeline-Preserving Speech-to-Speech Translation
items.summary: Speech-to-speech translation (S2ST) increasingly preserves what is said and how it sounds, but not necessarily when speech and silence occur. We present TransDubber, an end-to-end autoregressive system that learns this temporal structure directly from aligned target waveforms, without inference-time frame-level timing control or post-hoc temporal correction.

items.title: Behavioral Steering of Vision-Language-Action Models in the Low-Parameter Regime
items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) is increasingly used to adapt pretrained vision-language-action models (VLAs). To investigate how little trainable capacity such steering requires and how much pretrained capability can be retained, we freeze an OpenVLA-OFT 7B policy and optimize TinyLoRA adapters with 8 to 384 trainable parameters using either policy-gradient RL (GRPO) or evolutionary search (CMA-ES).

items.title: WorldSketch: Sketching World Models for Zero-Shot Mobile Manipulation
items.summary: In this paper, we propose WorldSketch, a new paradigm for agentic robotics in which a VLM constructs a world model rather than generating robot actions. The VLM acts as an agent that actively queries perception tools to build and visually validate a minimal kinematic world model, capturing only task-relevant objects, their interaction geometry, and possible motions.

items.title: MESSPa: A Multi-modal Embodiment Stimulation Shoulder Pad for Preserving the Sense of Agency in a Detachable Robotic Arm
items.summary: Wearable robots such as supernumerary robotic limbs (SRLs) can augment human capability, but their effectiveness depends strongly on the operator's sense of embodiment, comprising the sense of agency (SoA) and the sense of ownership (SoO).

items.title: Knowing Where to Look: Interactive Object Search via Spatial-Semantic Fusion
items.summary: When searching for an object, humans naturally combine semantic intuition - reasoning about where the object is likely to be stored - with geometric awareness of what parts of the space are visible, occluded, or unexplored.

items.title: TacMind: Benchmarking and Modeling Tactile Interaction States for Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: However, existing tactile manipulation studies are often developed and evaluated within specific task settings, making it difficult to systematically compare how tactile information contributes under different interaction conditions. We therefore propose an action-conditioned latent predictive world model that integrates tactile history and learns a tactile state through prediction of future tactile latents.

items.title: Behavior Graphs: Unsupervised Graph Structures for Interpreting Robot Deployment Data
items.summary: Data flywheels promise continuous improvement via insights from deployment data. To make deployment data easier to analyze and act on, we propose behavior graphs, which compress policy rollouts into a single interpretable, directed graph. As the number of deployed robots grows, behavior graphs lend structure to high-dimensional policy rollouts and make deployment data easier to interpret and reason about.

items.title: Emergent Control of Ant Learning Walks in a Mobile Robot
items.summary: Before foraging, desert ants perform learning walks (LWs) to acquire visual memories around their nest. Here, we test whether this mechanism can generate learning walks on a physical robot, despite the sensory and motor noise inherent to real-world conditions.

items.title: SPARK: Self-Correcting Embodied Memory via Physical Re-Observation
items.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems have seen growing adoption in embodied settings as language-queryable memories of the environment. To address this, we present SPARK, a corrective multi-episode framework for embodied RAG. Overall, SPARK demonstrates the value of correcting embodied memory through targeted re-observation, particularly as embodied systems scale and the risk of accumulated errors increases.

items.title: Teach, Abstract, Apply: A Framework for Dialogue-Driven Task Learning with Collaborative Robots
items.summary: Collaborative robots (cobots) are designed to be safer and more interactive than traditional industrial robots, share the same workspace as humans, and assist them in a range of shop-floor tasks such as palletization, joint assembly, and part inspection.

items.title: Does Validation Loss Predict Real-Robot Success? Evidence from Four Imitation-Learning Policies on a Low-Cost Arm
items.summary: Held-out validation loss is the standard offline signal for choosing checkpoints and comparing models, but its relation to closed-loop success on a real robot is rarely measured. We score 82 checkpoints on 25 held-out demonstrations, with each policy's training loss and with the error of the actions it outputs, and compare the scores with 930 bench rollouts.

items.title: Supervised Autonomous Bimanual Suction and Cauterization for Bleeding Control in Low Grade Splenic Trauma
items.summary: In this work, we present a supervised autonomous bimanual robotic framework for injury cauterization (eletrosurgical coagulation) in low-grade splenic trauma. Evaluated on a novel, cannulated ex vivo splenic hemorrhage model, the system achieved an average bleeding surface cauterization coverage of 82.9% across seven distinct injuries.

items.title: Anchor 1: Precise and Stable Humanoid Control for Whole-Body Manipulation
items.summary: Humanoid controllers have acquired increasingly diverse motor skills, yet translating these capabilities into precise and stable whole-body manipulation remains challenging. Introducing Anchor 1, a whole-body controller for precise and stable whole-body manipulation, together with a benchmark spanning diverse coordination demands.

items.title: Learning to Live: A Step Toward Lifelong Embodied Intelligence
items.summary: Embodied agents are usually organized around individual tasks, yet the physical world keeps changing between tasks and during execution. We introduce LIFE (Lifelong Intelligence from Experience), a framework in which a robot observes continuously, remembers selectively, and turns experience into new capabilities.

items.title: Scaling Trusted Autonomy: Towards Generally Capable Verifiable Robots
items.summary: Robots powered by foundation models are increasingly able to interpret open-ended language, recognize unfamiliar objects, and operate across diverse environments. This thesis argues that scaling trusted autonomy requires a neurosymbolic approach that unifies the generality of learned models with symbolic structure for robust robot behavior.

items.title: From Concepts to Actual Causes: Toward Closing the Concept-Malfunction Gap in Robot Foundation Models
items.summary: Post-incident analysis of a robot foundation model poses a singular causal question: which internal components caused this failure, and to what degree? Mechanistic interpretability (MI), however, establishes general causal claims by decoding the concepts a policy has learned, yet knowing which concepts are encoded is insufficient for identifying the actual cause of a specific incident.

items.title: DEPLOY-RL: Active Boundary Discovery and Conservative Certification for Deployable Reinforcement Learning in Safety-Critical Continuous Processes
items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) policies often outperform classical controllers in simulation, yet rarely reach production in safety-critical processes. The barrier is that there is no principled way to answer "Is this policy safe to deploy?" with statistical guarantees.

items.title: Decomposing Irregular Time Series into Interpretable Temporal Patterns with Mixture-of-Experts
items.summary: Irregularly-spaced sequential data, such as transaction logs, encode multi-scale temporal structure that is critical for prediction but difficult to recover explicitly with standard sequence models, which often trade interpretability for performance.

items.title: C3: Speech-Guided KV Retrieval for Long-Context SpeechLLM Inference
items.summary: Speech language models encode audio at a much higher rate than text, causing the KV cache to dominate the memory, bandwidth, and decoding cost of long-form generation. KV retrieval can reduce per-step access by attending to only a query-dependent subset of the cache, but existing methods are designed primarily for text and do not account for the structure of audio attention.

items.title: Cyber-physical attack detection approaches in the wide-area measurement system
items.summary: Improving situational awareness within the Smart Grid is an effective preventive measure to detect potential anomalies, and avoid their adverse consequences.

items.title: RaMMOBO: Random Max-Margin Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization
items.summary: Multi-objective Bayesian optimization (MOBO) maximizes $M$ expensive black-box objectives with the goal of approximating the Pareto set, whose objective vectors cannot be improved in one component without sacrificing another. We introduce random max-margin multi-objective Bayesian optimization (RaMMOBO), whose acquisition function lower-bounds EHVI while requiring only linear cost in $M$ to evaluate.

items.title: A Framework for Task-Agnostic Counterfactual Fairness in Transformers through Activation Steering
items.summary: Mechanistic interpretability (MI) is a growing body of work that measures meaningful causal effects of activations on model output by identifying human-interpretable features encoded in model activations. However, counterfactual fairness (CF) methods have not been systematically adapted to this setting of intervening on interpretable mechanisms in transformers.

items.title: Quantization of Large Models with Weight Outliers and Sparsity
items.summary: Post-training quantization (PTQ) reduces the memory burden of large model deployment by casting the high precision trained weights to fewer bits. To compensate for quantization error, the present contribution decomposes the original trained weights into a quantized matrix, a low-rank component, and a sparse matrix that accounts for outlier rows in the weights.

items.title: OCELOT: Planetary-Scale Species Distribution Modeling with Satellite Foundation Embeddings
items.summary: Large-scale repositories of species observations now contain billions of occurrence records from around the world, but these sightings cluster heavily in human-accessible areas.

items.title: DELBERT-2: Pretrained Fingerprint Language Models for DEL Protein Binder Prediction
items.summary: We present DELBERT-2, a pretrained fingerprint language model that converts sparse molecular fingerprints into unified token sequences using a ModernBERT encoder trained with masked language modelling on 2.5M molecules from the AIRCHECK DEL corpus.

items.title: KINDER: Kernel-based Independence for Fair Representation Learning via Prototype-space Erasure
items.summary: Concept erasure is a prominent approach to achieving fairness in machine learning through the removal of sensitive attributes from learned representations. Prior concept erasure methods typically define debiasing indirectly through the failure of a chosen adversary, probe, or fairness penalty, which makes the target of erasure dependent on a particular decoder family or optimization setup.

items.title: IsoAlign: Isoform-Aware DNA-Protein Alignment via Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures
items.summary: Genomic foundation models (GFMs) have emerged as a powerful paradigm for learning DNA sequence representations, yet existing self-supervised pretraining strategies overlook alternative splicing and underperform compared to specialized models.

items.title: ProLand: A New Infeasible Manifold Optimization Method for LoRA Fine-Tuning
items.summary: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) enables parameter-efficient fine-tuning but can suffer from redundant basis directions. Landing methods allow temporarily infeasible iterates to explore a neighborhood of the manifold while progressively restoring orthogonality without per-step retractions.

items.title: Interpretable structural temperature scaling for calibrating graph neural networks and point-cloud segmentation
items.summary: Graph-aware calibrators make graph neural networks (GNNs) more trustworthy by predicting a temperature for each node, usually with auxiliary networks whose decisions are hard to inspect.

items.title: FB-MOAC: A Reinforcement Learning Algorithm for Forward-Backward Markov Decision Processes
items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms are effective in solving problems that can be modeled as Markov decision processes (MDPs). However, several important problems in different scenarios including stochastic control and network systems exhibit both a forward and a backward dynamics.

items.title: Output-Aware Block Influence: Jacobian-Lens Weighting for Depth Pruning
items.summary: Depth pruning removes entire transformer blocks and therefore depends on a reliable criterion for identifying which blocks can be removed. Block Influence (BI) ranks blocks by how minimally they rotate the hidden state.

items.title: Quantifying Local and Global Fidelity of Nonlinear Embeddings
items.summary: Dimension reduction methods are chosen by a common claim: t-SNE and UMAP preserve local structure, and PCA preserves global structure. Checking it on given data takes local and global scores on one scale and a test that compares two maps. Its value at k = 10 is the local fidelity L, and its mean over 30 to 50 percent of the data is the global fidelity G.

items.title: Automated Theorem Generation in First-Order Logic by Construction from Triangular Standard Contradictions
items.summary: Automated theorem generation (ATG) seeks to construct new theorems rather than merely prove given conjectures. We propose a constructive framework for ATG in first-order logic based on triangular standard contradictions. Extending the previously developed $\Delta_1$ generator, we introduce seven methods, $\Delta_2$--$\Delta_8$, forming a unified family of eight theorem-generation methods.

items.title: A generative foundation model for computational brain imaging
items.summary: Computational brain imaging is constrained by a mismatch between increasingly diverse tasks and scarce, heterogeneous clinical data. This paper proposes BrainGFM, a generative foundation model that extends knowledge transfer beyond representation reuse through a reusable and reconfigurable brain-imaging prior.

items.title: Taurus: LLM-in-the-Loop CT Annotation Matches Coding Agents at Half the Cost
items.summary: Dense labels of the aorta in CT are slow to draw, and the public aortic CT datasets that could stand in for them each label different structures under their own conventions. We asked whether such a model labels these scans better as a free-form agent that writes its own segmentation code, or inside a harness, where an automated pass labels the scan and the model reviews the result.

items.title: OmniPiano: Diverse Dexterous Piano-Playing Challenges for Standard, Robust, Safe, and Multi-Agent RL
items.summary: Dexterous robotic manipulation remains a major challenge in robotics, exemplified by piano playing, which requires coordinated control of fingers and provides a demanding testbed for reinforcement learning (RL). To address this gap, we introduce OmniPiano, a benchmark that provides one to up to five Shadow Hands and supports standard, robust, safe, and multi-agent RL within a shared piano-playing task family.

items.title: RE-SciVQA: Improving Scientific VQA With Context-Relevant Retrieval and Lightweight MLLM Adaptation
items.summary: A deep understanding of scientific literature often relies on interpreting figures that contain key information beyond the main text. Existing works on Scientific Visual Question Answering rely on resource-intensive training pipelines that are often inaccessible and require large computational resources.

items.title: From Cross-Section to Cross-Omics: Conditional Cell Nucleus Image Editing in Spatial Transcriptomics
items.summary: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) platforms simultaneously measure gene expression and capture cell nucleus images at single-cell resolution. A fundamental property of tissue preparation introduces a confounding relationship between the two measurement modalities: sectioning a three-dimensional tissue into a thin slice produces a two-dimensional cross-section whose area depends on the cutting angle.

items.title: MemU-Bench: Benchmarking GUI Agents on Long-Horizon User Interactions
items.summary: Existing Graphical User Interface (GUI) benchmarks predominantly rely on precise and stateless user instructions. Alongside Success Rate, we incorporate Interaction Efficiency (IE) and Success weighted by Path Length (SPL) to expose agents that succeed by exhaustively searching across different applications rather than by \emph{genuinely recalling} the history.

items.title: Neurons Are All You Need
items.summary: Inspired by this research, we sought to demonstrate memory transfer of persistent memory between AI model instances, leveraging a neurocentric version of memory. By structurally separating computation from persistent memory, NURESA enables autonomous memory accumulation and consolidation into transferable stores of memory registers.

items.title: AuroraWorld: Structured 4D World Modeling for Exo-to-Ego Video Generation in Robot Manipulation
items.summary: Egocentric observations provide a robot-centric view of manipulation processes, capturing contact interactions and object-state changes that are important for visuomotor policy learning but difficult to observe from external cameras. items.title: Reimagining Text-to-SQL: A Survey of Large Language Model Architectures and Strategies
items.summary: Text-to-SQL systems translate natural language questions into executable SQL queries, democratizing access to relational data. Early approaches relied on handcrafted rules and template matching, while subsequent neural methods introduced encoder-decoder architectures, schema linking, and constrained decoding to handle increasingly complex queries.

items.title: PatchScout: Thematic Web Data Collection via Information Foraging
items.summary: Researchers often need web corpora that are not answers to a single query, but reusable collections of documents spanning many decentralized sources. We refer to this problem as thematic web data collection: assembling semantically relevant documents that share a common theme but are scattered across heterogeneous and structurally disconnected regions of the web.

items.title: Early Stopping in Large Reasoning Models: A Survey and Empirical Audit of Efficiency and Reliability
items.summary: Large reasoning models can improve accuracy by generating longer reasoning traces, but some of this computation may be unnecessary. We evaluate different methods across five reasoning models on mathematical and scientific reasoning, code generation, and factuality tasks by using a shared rollout replay protocol.

items.summary: An online retailer launching a perishable product bids for sponsored-search clicks, discounts a bundle with an always-stocked staple and displays its remaining stock, which raises willingness to pay.

items.summary: Fuzzy clustering provides a robust framework for handling ambiguous and overlapping data boundaries, yet its traditional formulation generates entirely dense membership assignments that limit noise resilience and prevent estimating the true number of clusters, when it is unknown.
